sections.overview: Intoshia variabili is an orthonectid parasite of marine flatworms, with a documented host now called Graffiellus croceus.
sections.identification: Its adult forms are minute and structurally reduced; a 2020 study reported the smallest known orthonectid genome at 15.3 Mbp.
sections.habitat: The parasitic stage inhabits its flatworm host; older studies examined it in Macrorhynchus crocea under a former host identification.
sections.diet: Adult orthonectids lack a digestive system, while the host-dwelling plasmodium is the feeding stage.
sections.behavior: Male and female adults emerge from the host; comparative work has investigated how that emergence occurs.
sections.reproduction: After leaving the host, the brief adult stage reproduces sexually; species-specific details remain sparse.
sections.ecology: Its congener I. linei is included with it in comparative studies of orthonectid mitochondrial genomes. I. linei parasitizes the ribbon worm Lineus ruber, whereas I. variabili parasitizes flatworms.
sections.conservation: The literature located concerns anatomy, parasitism and genomics, not population trends or a conservation assessment.
